forecasts.label: Capital expenditure

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Bradford's 2026/27 budget includes £78m of exceptional financial support; 2027/28 forecast needs none
news_drafts.lead:
Bradford's budget for 2026/27 includes a £78m capitalisation direction, according to the annual report of its external auditor for 2025/26. A capitalisation direction is government permission to treat day-to-day spending as capital spending, so it can be paid for by borrowing or asset sales. The auditor writes: "In 2026/27 the Council is reliant on Exceptional Financial Support through a Capitalisation Direction of £78m to balance the budget."

The council's refreshed medium term financial strategy shows an overall reduction of £175m in the level of exceptional financial support, which is government permission to borrow or sell assets to cover day-to-day spending. It forecasts that no such support will be needed to balance the 2027/28 budget. The 2026/27 budget also carries a £50m savings target. The council received capitalisation directions of £313m between 2023/24 and 2025/26.

The auditor states that "Since 2023/24 the Council has required Exceptional Financial Support (EFS) to set a balanced budget." It describes this as evidence of a significant weakness in how the council plans to bridge funding gaps. The auditor recommends that the council set future balanced budgets that do not rely on the support.

news_drafts.headline: Bradford forecasts no exceptional financial support in 2027-28, against £81m in its original plan
news_drafts.lead:
Bradford Council anticipates that 2027-28 will be the first financial year since 2022-23 in which it operates without exceptional financial support, which is government permission to borrow or sell assets to cover day-to-day spending. Papers for the Corporate Overview and Scrutiny Committee on 12 November put the forecast for that support in 2027-28 at nil, against an original plan of £81m.

The council says it has relied on a cumulative estimated £391m of the support over the four years from 2023-24 to 2026-27, against an original planned total of £570m. For 2026-27 the forecast is £78m, against an original £129m. In 2024-25 the support came in at £120m, £20m below the original request of £140m. In 2025-26 it came in at £113m, against £127.1m requested. The 2023-24 figure matched the £80m request. The original-plan rows in the report's Table 1 add to £579m, not the £570m shown as the total.

The report says the 2027-28 forecast depends on delivery of the council's recovery programme, the savings proposals in the paper, and additional funding expected from the government's Fair Funding review. The original plan also included £42m of support for 2028-29, and the current forecast for that year is nil.

news_drafts.headline: Bradford forecasts £391m of exceptional support since 2023-24, against £570m planned
news_drafts.lead:
Bradford Council expects 2027-28 to be the first financial year since 2022-23 in which it can operate without exceptional financial support, which is government permission to borrow or sell assets to cover day-to-day spending. Papers for the Executive meeting on 3 November put the cumulative support from 2023-24 onwards at £391m on the current forecast, against an original plan of £570m. The paper says the council "has relied upon cumulative EFS of £391 million to support its revenue budget".

By year, the support was £80m in 2023-24. In 2024-25 it came out at £120m, £20m below the original request of £140m. In 2025-26 it came out at £113m, which was £14.1m below the £127.1m requested. For 2026-27 the council forecasts £78m, against an original plan of £129m.

The paper says the council "is currently forecasting a return to a financially sustainable position from 2027-28, at which point reliance on EFS is no longer expected". It links that expectation to delivery of the recovery programme, the savings proposals in the report, and the additional funding expected from the Fair Funding review.

findings.paper_title: DOC R1 - CBMDC Auditor's Annual Report 2025-26 - Final
findings.headline: Auditor records four of five prior-year internal control recommendations still outstanding for 2026/27, with one addressed in 2025/26
findings.detail: The auditor identified no new internal control recommendations from its 2025/26 audit of the Council.
findings.matters: Outstanding internal control recommendations are a control risk a finance director can compare against their own audit tracker.
findings.figures: Five prior-year recommendations; one addressed in 2025/26; four remaining for 2026/27
findings.quote: one recommendation had been addressed during 2025/26 and four remained to be addressed in 2026/27.

findings.paper_title: DOC R1 - CBMDC Auditor's Annual Report 2025-26 - Final
findings.headline: Local Government Financial Settlement increased the Council's core spending power by 47%
findings.detail: The paper says the Council reported this increase after the Fair Funding Review and the Local Government Financial Settlement. It is cited as part of the improved financial plan.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council can compare the settlement's effect on core spending power against their own settlement change.
findings.quote: The Council reported the settlement increased its core spending power by 47%.

findings.paper_title: DOC R1 - CBMDC Auditor's Annual Report 2025-26 - Final
findings.headline: Ofsted rates Bradford children's services as 'Requires improvement to be good', up from 'Inadequate' in 2022, but the Statutory Direction remains in place for 2025/26
findings.detail: The auditor records the Ofsted inspection outcome as evidence of strong improvement, which led to the removal of monitoring visits. The auditor still records a significant weakness, because the Statutory Direction and intervention under the Commissioner continued through 2025/26.
findings.matters: A lender or finance director can see that the Council's governance significant weakness depends on the Statutory Direction, not on the inspection rating.
findings.figures: Overall effectiveness rated 'Requires improvement to be good' in 2026, against 'Inadequate' in 2022
findings.quote: the Statutory Direction has remained in place during 2025/26

findings.paper_title: DOC R1 - CBMDC Auditor's Annual Report 2025-26 - Final
findings.headline: Auditor reports the Governance and Audit Committee received one internal audit report during 2025/26
findings.detail: The auditor's governance commentary says this did not enable the Committee to discharge its responsibilities, and raises an other recommendation. The Head of Internal Audit gave reasonable assurance, except for one issue.
findings.matters: Limited internal audit reporting to the audit committee is a control gap a finance director at another council can check against their own reporting cycle.
findings.figures: One internal audit report received by the Committee during 2025/26
findings.quote: During 2025/26 the Committee only received one internal audit report

findings.paper_title: DOC R1 - CBMDC Auditor's Annual Report 2025-26 - Final
findings.headline: Auditor issues an unqualified opinion on the Council's 2025/26 financial statements, and reports no additional significant weaknesses in value for money arrangements for the year
findings.detail: The auditor reports continuing significant weaknesses in financial sustainability and governance, carried forward from 2024/25. The auditor records no new significant weaknesses for 2025/26, and the improving economy criterion has no significant weakness.
findings.matters: A lender and a finance director can see the Council's audit status: an unqualified opinion, with the same two significant weaknesses carried over and none added.
findings.figures: Unqualified opinion issued 14 October 2026; two continuing significant weaknesses (financial sustainability and governance)
findings.quote: Our work in 2025/26 has not identified any additional significant weaknesses
